evidence: README 'Before / after' (plain baseline, mobile 6x n=3, old tools: fps 63.7 -> 69.5, frames >20 ms 115 -> 91, disjoint) and 'Visual / behaviour parity'
notes: Drafted by the fix owner. Counts are predicted from the code until the runner calibrates them on aw1-10c (patch.diff is stacked on aw1-10c).

hero.why: The hero exit: y 0 to the end of .hero-track (200vh), where .pain starts.

exitOpacityWrites.why: Baseline s (JS 4163 plain, 4384 on aw1-10c) writes --exit-opacity on .hero every engine frame. In CSS mode the patch writes none.

heroPointerEventsWrites.why: Baseline s writes style.pointerEvents every frame. The patch writes it only when its IntersectionObserver flips (track bottom crosses 1.05 viewport heights).

cueFilterAnimations.why: On phones the patched cue blur is a scroll-driven animation on .scroll-float. The baseline only has the idle bob there (transform).
cueFilterAnimations.name: hero-exit-blur

copyOpacityAnimations.why: Counts only the patch exit animation (name filter). A selector-only count was flaky (3 vs 0): the baseline copy has other opacity animations inside it.
copyOpacityAnimations.name: hero-exit-copy

mechanism.why: Phones are in CSS mode from mount. Predicted baseline: about 1 write per 100 px step over about 930 px of exit progress.
Desktop switches to CSS mode when the entrance ends (about 1.8 s after load, d). The runner's settle is assumed to outlast it.
Patched: one write when the IntersectionObserver flips near the end of the exit, at most one more if the scroll comes back.
Proves the CSS path is live on phones (supported and attached). Without it the JS fallback runs and no-exit-opacity-writes fails too.
The copy fade runs as a compositor-eligible opacity animation, not through an inherited custom property.

parity.why: The cue fade moves from .scroll-cue to .scroll-float on phones, so its opacity is compared in the README visual check (product of both), not here.

gain.why: The plain-baseline A/B moved per-frame cost (frames >20 ms, fps), not LoAF. The iPhone hero window (y 0-900) is the device check (iPhone-led, wave 2).

experiments.why: v1 keyframes used animated custom properties: on Safari 26 the cue stayed at opacity 0 (P3). Chrome parity likely passes, so this needs the iPhone.
v2 with the original local names, functionally the same as 04.
v2 on the plain baseline (the measured n=3 A/B).
No exit blur, a visual change on purpose (attribution only). The cue filter animation is missing.
P3: 09 plus the people-o snap and clip-path reveal on phones (F-032). Hero checks unchanged, heading layouts during the expand 25-30 per step to 0-4.
v2 restacked on aw1-10c (patch.diff). The gain is still to be measured on the iPhone hero window and Chrome.
